title: Field protocol v1 describe manifest (Field to core)
description: The single manifest frame a Field emits on standard output in response to a describe request. It is the Field's complete self-declaration: negotiated protocol, registered identity, capability slices, source-key derivation, identity anchors, deletion authority, cursor format, credential requirement, known limitations, and the exhaustive list of connector-prefixed properties the Field may emit. Core snapshots the manifest per configured Field; an incompatible change to a declared property or cursor format fails the next sync closed instead of silently retyping notebook data.

protocol_version.description: The single version the Field selected from the versions core offered.

driver.description: Stable connector driver name, matching the configured Field's driver.

property_prefix.description: The registered property prefix. Absent for a Field contributing none; never null, so an omitted member and an explicit null are not two spellings of the same thing. Before this revision the member was required-but-nullable, which meant an omitted member and 'null' were indistinguishable failure modes at best and, at worst, an omitted key silently meant 'contributes no prefix' while null was read some other way.

declared_properties.description: Exhaustive declaration of the connector-prefixed properties this Field may emit. Core rejects any prefixed property a record carries that is absent here, and rejects a value whose JSON shape contradicts the declared scalar type or cardinality. This replaces spelling-based type inference for declared properties. Unprefixed shared properties are never declared here: they belong to the closed A1 shared registry and take their type from it.

capabilities.description: The source-object slices this release actually supports. Narrowing is allowed and must be visible here and in status output; it is never an implicit claim of full vendor coverage.

identity_anchors.description: Identity-anchor namespaces this Field may emit. Declaring an anchor never makes it part of the exact-source key.

limitations.description: Known permission, history, or coverage limits a user must be told about.

name.description: Full prefixed property name, beginning with this manifest's property_prefix. Core verifies the prefix against the manifest and against the A1 registry.

list_semantics.description: Required for a list, forbidden for a scalar. 'set' is sorted and deduplicated by normalized value; 'ordered' preserves the source or role order the Field emits.

object_kind.description: Connector-local object-kind token, also used as the object-kind namespace inside source_identity.

note_type.description: Primary Note type this slice maps to. Must be one of A1's eleven approved primary Note types; the protocol does not restate that vocabulary and core validates against the A1 registry.

sourceKeyDeclaration.description: How this Field derives the portable exact-source key. The derivation is declared so two instances of the same connector against the same upstream authority produce identical keys, and so a reviewer can confirm the scope is non-secret and label-independent.

scope_shape.description: Non-secret illustrative shape of the scope this Field produces, for review.

scope_depends_on_field_label.description: Must be false. A portable scope derives from the upstream authority or account, never from the user's local Field label.

substitutes_for_source_key.description: Must be false. An anchor may relate graph entities; it never identifies an upstream object for reconciliation.

protected_channel_required.description: Whether the Field needs the protected credential channel. A Field that declares 'none' must declare false and core delivers no grant.

scopes.description: Least-privilege read-only scope tokens the Field needs.

refresh_owner.description: Which side renews expiring credential material.

writes_to_source.description: Must be false. Collection is read-only; no Field writes to its source system.

window_supported.description: Whether the Field honours a bounded time window in the collection request.

deletion.description: Deletion authority. 'tombstones' authorizes explicit delete records; 'snapshot' authorizes removal by proven absence inside a declared scope after a complete snapshot run. Core rejects any deletion signal a Field has not declared authority for.

allOf.description: Snapshot deletion authority requires the Field to actually support snapshot mode.
